input: After the rig came back from a day-long power-off, Suwayomi is acting like it lost everything: inside the container, /home/suwayomi/.local/share/Tachidesk/downloads/ is EMPTY and downloads/thumbnails is 'No such file or directory'; the log has recurring java.io.FileNotFoundException .../thumbnails/<id>.tmp for every manga in the library. But on the rig HOST, /mnt/nas-manga (CIFS mount of the NAS manga share) is healthy and contains mangas/ + thumbnails/, and the DB still says 279 chapters downloaded. docker inspect suwayomi shows StartedAt=2026-08-01T14:25:47Z and both binds with Propagation=rprivate; `systemctl show 'mnt-nas\x2dmanga.mount' -p ActiveEnterTimestamp` says 'Sat 2026-08-01 10:25:52 EDT'. Host timezone is EDT. What happened, what's the risk if I leave it, and what's the immediate + durable fix?

Confusing one on mini: this morning's 10:23 verification run failed the crit check alert-healthchecks-none-down with output 'down_checks=verification-mini' — but when I query the Healthchecks API myself a couple of minutes later, all 16 checks are up, including verification-mini. Context from the journals: yesterday's (Aug 01) daily verification run logged 'verify-cycle.sh: 201/296 passed, 95 failed (8 crit)' at 10:43 (the rig had just come back from a long outage) and then at 10:45:18 'verification.service: Failed with result timeout'. The unit has TimeoutStartSec=30min and pings its Healthchecks dead-man via an ExecStartPost curl. Healthchecks flipped verification-mini down at 2026-08-02T02:26:49Z and up at 2026-08-02T14:25:01Z. Was this morning's crit a false positive? What actually happened, and what's the underlying design weakness?

The verification runner on mini has an LLM auto-triage step: it sends each failed check's JSON plus a skill prompt to a model on the rig and writes verdicts. Over the last 5 daily runs, 68 of 75 verdicts are the hardcoded fallback {"confidence": 0.0, "escalate": true, "diagnosis": "triage failed — model did not return valid JSON"} with likely_cause 'no JSON object in response'. Yet the dedicated guard check llm-triage-completion-e2e — built specifically to catch triage breakage — passes every single day. The guard's probe sends the one-liner 'Reply with the JSON object {"ok":true} and nothing else.' with max_tokens=600 and asserts only non-empty content. Real triage uses the same model (a large reasoning model) and the same max_tokens=600, but with the full skill prompt + failed-check JSON. Why does real triage fail ~91% of the time while its guard stays green, and how should the guard and/or triage change?

The convergence tripwire ansible-site-converged-mini is permanently red: the nightly ansible-pull on BOTH mini and rig always ends changed=1, and it's always the same task — 'state : Apply dotfiles with chezmoi (glue-04)'. That task runs `chezmoi init --apply git@forgejo:home/dotfiles.git` with `become: false` (so it runs as btabaska), guarded by `creates: "{{ ansible_env.HOME }}/.local/share/chezmoi/.git"`. The play in site.yml sets `become: true` at play level. /home/btabaska/.local/share/chezmoi/.git exists on both hosts and has since Jul 28. chezmoi itself reports an empty diff. Why does the task re-run and report changed every night, what's the collateral damage, and what's the fix?

In the mini journaling loop (memos + n8n journal-analyze workflow), memo 36 is tagged #journal but never received its AI reflection comment, while the other three #journal memos from the same two-week window each got exactly one. n8n's execution history shows TWO executions matching memo 36's timestamps, both finishing 'success' in ~24ms — genuinely analyzed memos take ~3s. One more oddity: memo 36's created and updated timestamps differ by 43 seconds, while the analyzed memos all have created == updated. What's the root cause, and how would I prove it from the workflow and n8n's own data?

The verification LLM-triage layer on mini has produced nothing useful for days: every triage-YYYY-MM-DD.md since Jul 15 contains only stubs like "triage failed — model did not return valid JSON / LLM request failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found" with escalate:true. The odd part: bin/llm-triage.sh in the repo looks correct — it defaults to the rig llama-swap endpoint (:9292/v1, model qwen3.6-35b-a3b) which is healthy — and the script's llm_up() availability gate isn't tripping the incident/WoL path either, so nothing ever alerted. Root cause? How do I confirm it end to end?

On the rig, every LiteLLM request using a virtual API key suddenly returns 503 with {'type':'no_db_connection','message':'the authentication database is temporarily unreachable'}. /health/readiness is 503 but /health/liveliness is 200, and llm.tabaska.us still answers 200 through caddy, so the dashboards look fine. 'docker ps' shows the litellm-db postgres container as 'Up 25 hours (healthy)'. This started overnight, during the same window the rig was having other filesystem trouble. What's the real state, the root cause chain, and how do I confirm — including why docker ps disagrees with reality?

Komga on the nas has two libraries, Comics and Manga, and the API shows both configured scanInterval=EVERY_6H, unavailable=False. Comics scans fine every 6 hours. But /volume1/manga holds 279 downloaded chapters (newest .cbz dated Jul 27) and Komga's Manga library still shows just 1 series with 1 book, indexed Jul 23 — nothing new for days. The container log repeats every 6h: "LibraryScanScheduler : Periodic scan for library: Manga" -> "TaskEmitter : Sending task: ScanLibrary(libraryId='0R33RZ4PAF7JC', ...)" -> "TaskHandler : Cannot execute task ScanLibrary(...): Library does not exist". Meanwhile the API lists the Manga library with id 0R3629KVZ4AKY. Our chain checks (suwayomi-feeds-komga, komga-libraries-consumer) are green. What's the root cause, the quickest fix, and why did monitoring miss it?

The check spent-enabled-timers on mini flags 'SPENT_ENABLED=verification.timer' in the 10:23 daily sweep — and it has done so every daily run for 14 straight days. The check's logic: `systemctl list-timers --all`, flag any enabled timer where NEXT is 'n/a' but LAST is set (the signature of a timer that fired once and will never fire again). But every time I inspect that timer interactively in the afternoon it's perfectly healthy: NEXT=Mon 10:15, LAST=today 10:15, OnCalendar daily. An off-schedule audit sweep at 13:01 also passes the same check. verification.timer triggers verification.service, a long-running oneshot that takes ~10 minutes. What's the false-positive mechanism and how should the check be fixed?

The homelab-alerts ntfy topic is getting flooded: 'NAS services down — Still down after compose up: stash', identical message every ~15 minutes from 01:45 through past 10:15. On the nas, `docker ps` shows stash 'Up 3 weeks'. The stash-serving verification check is also failing with empty output. But here's the thing — Stash itself seems fine: I can log into the web UI normally, and a GraphQL query WITH an ApiKey answers in milliseconds. I did enable authentication on Stash a couple of weeks ago. What's actually broken here, why does the self-heal never help, and what needs to change (app, checks, self-heal, alerting)?

Sonarr on the nas has 13 queue records wedged for 3+ days: 12 episodes of one season pack (Better.Off.Ted S02 REPACK) plus one other episode, all 'completed / importPending' with the warning 'No files found are eligible for import in /seedbox/tv/<release>'. On the seedbox, deluge RPC reports both torrents 100% 'Seeding' with save_path=/home/hd34/btabaska/files/tv. But `ls` of that directory on the seedbox shows NEITHER release present — nothing matching anywhere under files/ — and the NAS-side rclone mount of the seedbox agrees. unpackerr independently logs 'stat err: ... no such file or directory' for the same paths. How can deluge report 'Seeding 100%' when the files don't exist, what's the root cause class, and what's the remediation?

NAS arr stack is churning hard today: Radarr's queue has ~13 stuck items with rejections like 'Not an upgrade for existing movie file. Existing quality: Bluray-1080p. New Quality WEBDL-1080p', new grabs keep appearing roughly hourly in Radarr and every ~30 minutes in Sonarr for titles we ALREADY own, and each grab burns 3-16GB of seedbox disk/bandwidth. Worse, a few movies imported fresh files today — Aliens (1986) and Chinatown (1974) now show Russian/English audio languages and Hotel Transylvania 3 shows Bulgarian/English, so the family is getting Russian-audio playback in Plex. Two more queue items sit at 0% with 0 seeds for days and never get cleaned up. What is the likely root cause of this whole pattern, and how would I confirm it via the arr APIs?

I want my Audiobookshelf audiobooks and podcasts (libraries on the NAS at /volume1/audiobooks and /volume1/podcasts) synced onto my iPod Classic, which docks on the rig — and they need to land in the iPod's NATIVE Audiobooks and Podcasts menus, not mixed into Music. This has to coexist with the existing Rhythmbox music sync on the rig. Give me the full plan: share/mount plumbing from the NAS, how tracks end up in the right iPod menus, staging vs push design, the DSM and iPod-database gotchas you'd expect, back-catalog handling, and monitoring.

The NAS is chronically I/O-saturated: 15-min load sits at 17-22 against a quiet baseline around 2.8, CPU utilisation is low (it's iowait), and there's no RAID scrub or resync running. Knock-on damage: lidarr's 50 most recent error-log entries are ALL SQLite 'database is locked', soularr keeps fatal-exiting, `docker logs` on one container hangs for minutes, and CWA keeps flapping unhealthy. It's a Synology DS920+, so assume the kernel may not support cgroup blkio I/O throttling. Walk me through how you'd actually find the writers, and your remediation plan with verification.

Two problems on mini that I think are related: a raw Hardcover JWT keeps appearing in journald every day, and NONE of my systemd OnFailure ntfy pages on mini are delivering — restic-backup, tv-torrent-cleanup and friends fail silently now. Weirdly, the verification checks that use the Hardcover API still pass. I suspect something is wrong inside /etc/verification/env. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing this: the likely root cause, the fix, whether the token needs rotating, how you'd prove paging works again, and how you'd guard against the whole class.

My NAS movie library has been growing Russian- and Bulgarian-dubbed copies of movies I already own, and radarr's recent grab history is almost entirely my local Bitmagnet DHT indexer — roughly hourly grabs; sonarr is grabbing from it every half hour too. Everything routes through Prowlarr. I want a plan that stops the junk at the source, cleans up what got imported and what's still in the download queues, and prevents regression — WITHOUT losing the ability to manually search Bitmagnet when I choose to.

mini suddenly can't reach anything on my IoT VLAN (192.168.20.0/24) — 100% packet loss to the Hue hub at 192.168.20.100 — while Home Assistant on a different host controls the same devices fine, so the devices themselves are up. Everything else on mini looks normal. The most recent change on mini was deploying the journaling stack (memos + n8n + faster-whisper) with docker compose. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing this, what state you'd be careful to preserve while fixing it, and how you'd guard against the class recurring.

Every night at exactly 00:00 the NAS drops a fresh ~23MB core dump in the /volume1 root, and the journal shows it comes from immich_server's bundled ffmpeg segfaulting — it's happened 5 nights running now, same time each night. Photos still browse fine. Walk me through how you would diagnose what keeps triggering this and how you'd resolve it durably WITHOUT deleting or risking any photo/video asset, plus how you'd verify the fix and monitor for recurrence.

The rig serves a Qwen3 reranker through llama-swap's /v1/rerank endpoint (port 9292) — it's what Open WebUI's hybrid RAG uses to rerank retrieved chunks. I want a check that catches it being green-but-broken: returning HTTP 200 with well-formed JSON while being completely useless at actual ranking. What request would you send and what's the pass criterion?

Our voice stack: Kokoro TTS runs on the rig (:8880, CPU image) and faster-whisper STT runs on the mini (:8010) — Open WebUI is wired to both, and OWUI's audio settings live in its database (PersistentConfig), not in the compose env. Design one verification check that proves the whole voice path actually works end to end, and tell me what would still slip through if you only health-checked the two containers.
